summary: Rows of records to open, pick or act on — an approval inbox, a list of files, "choose one of these" that is not a form field. One tab stop, arrow keys inside, a row can hold buttons.
useWhen: each row is one record read across — a label, a line under it, a badge — and the user opens one, or picks some
an inbox or a queue: rows that open a detail, with several selectable for one action on all of them
picking one item from many where the choice is not a form value — the file to preview, the run to show beside the list
rows carry their own small actions — dismiss, a Menu of more

useInstead.when: the rows have columns that are compared down — duration, owner, status side by side
useInstead.why: a List has no header and no columns; values meant to be scanned down a column belong in one

useInstead.when: the choice is a value submitted with a form
useInstead.why: a List's selection is not a form field: it has no name, no validation and no label for the question

useInstead.when: a short, static list of links with nothing to select — related pages, three recent items
useInstead.why: links in a list are one tab stop each, which is right for a handful and needs no grid

useInstead.when: the items are the app's own pages

none.use: the default — a press opens the row: its `href`, or `onAction`

single.use: pick one, as in a file list: a press selects, Enter or a double click opens

multiple.use: an inbox: a checkbox per row. A press opens the row while nothing is selected and toggles it once something is; Space selects from the keyboard

items.note: each item: `label` (the row's name), `description` (a second line, read with the name), `leading` (Avatar or Icon — decorative, hidden from assistive technology, so it must not carry meaning the label does not), `meta` (Badge or text at the end, not interactive), `href`, `isDisabled`

renderActions.note: at the end of each row; each needs an `aria-label` that names its row — "Dismiss Reconcile March invoices", not "Dismiss"

renderEmptyState.note: shown in a row of its own when `items` is empty

requires: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` — the list's name, such as the heading above it
a unique `id` on every item — selection is held by id
a string `label`, or `textValue` when the label is not text — typeahead matches it and it is the row's name
guarantees: a `grid` of `row`s, one `gridcell` each; `aria-multiselectable` in `multiple`, `aria-selected` on each row only when rows can be selected
one tab stop: ↑ and ↓ move between rows, Home and End go to the ends, typing jumps to a matching label, and Tab leaves the list
→ moves into a row's own buttons and ← back out, so row actions add no tab stops; ↑ and ↓ from a button move to the next row
pressing a button inside a row does its job only — it does not open or select the row
`href` rows are links through React Aria's router: an app's `RouterProvider` if it has one, the browser otherwise, with modified clicks opening a new tab
`multiple` gives each row a real Checkbox named "Select" and the row's label; a click on its box toggles once
a disabled item is skipped by the arrow keys and cannot be opened or selected
the description is read with the row's label
an empty list stays a named grid, with `renderEmptyState` in a row of its own
rows are at least 48px tall; long labels wrap and the meta stays at the row's end; the keyboard focus ring is drawn on the row
notes: in `multiple` a press opens the row until something is selected — the inbox convention. Say what the checkboxes are for with the batch action they feed, such as a TableBatchBar above the list
in a single-page app with history routing, wrap the app in React Aria's `RouterProvider` so `href` rows navigate without a page load. Hash routes need nothing
`leading` is hidden from assistive technology: an avatar's initials or an icon's meaning must be in the label or description too

antiPatterns.dont: <ul> of <li onClick> rows, or <div role="button"> per row
antiPatterns.why: clickable list items are not focusable or announced as actionable, and buttons per row are a tab stop each with no selection

antiPatterns.dont: a Table with one column and no header, to get selectable rows
antiPatterns.why: a table claims columns and a header to compare; a screen reader announces "1 column" and reads a header that is not there

antiPatterns.dont: a checkbox drawn in each row's label to show selection
antiPatterns.why: a drawn box is not a control: it cannot be clicked without opening the row and is not announced with the row
arrowed into from outside its row, a button named only "Dismiss" does not say which one it dismisses

antiPatterns.dont: an empty List that renders nothing, or a grid with no rows
antiPatterns.why: an empty grid is announced as "0 rows" and nothing else; the user is not told whether it is loading, filtered or empty
